column3: The Hebrew names silence and a singular vow without our; BSB says praise awaits and has our vows.
The Hebrew says all flesh; BSB says all people.
The Hebrew names words or matters of iniquities and says they prevailed; BSB names iniquities and frames their prevailing as when.
The Hebrew uses a participle for establishing mountains with His power; BSB addresses You and says formed.
The Hebrew uses a participle for stilling and repeats the roaring of seas and waves; BSB uses past stilled and varies roaring and pounding.
The Hebrew names Your signs and the outgoings of morning and evening; BSB says wonders, dawn, and sunset.
The Hebrew has God’s channel in the singular and their grain; BSB has streams and our grain.
The Hebrew says You have crowned and describes paths dripping fatness; BSB uses present crown and overflow with plenty.
The Hebrew describes the hills girding themselves with joy; BSB says they are robed with joy.
The Hebrew pictures pastures putting on flocks and valleys wrapping themselves in grain; BSB uses passive clothed and decked.
